full_text:
मध्य और पूर्वी यूरोप की कई सरकारें बिजली संरक्षण और ऊर्जा संकट को रोकने के लिए उपाय लागू कर रही हैं क्योंकि यूरोप की दूसरी सबसे बड़ी नदी, डेन्यूब नदी, जो 10 देशों से होकर बहती है, का जलस्तर रिकॉर्ड निचले स्तर पर पहुंच गया है, जिससे बिजली संयंत्र बंद होने के कगार पर पहुंच गए हैं।
पहली बार परमाणु ऊर्जा संयंत्र को बंद कर दिया गया है।
भारी बारिश की संभावना न होने के कारण आने वाले दिनों या हफ्तों में डेन्यूब नदी का जलस्तर बढ़ने की आशंका नहीं है। वहीं, क्षेत्र में भीषण गर्मी की लहर चल रही है, जिससे दिन का तापमान 38 डिग्री सेल्सियस से अधिक हो गया है और बिजली व पानी की खपत बढ़ गई है। 3 अगस्त को एक वीडियो संबोधन में प्रधानमंत्री पीटर मैग्यार ने कहा कि हंगरी अभूतपूर्व समय से गुजर रहा है और सबसे कठिन दिन अभी आने बाकी हैं। मैग्यार ने कहा कि अगर डेन्यूब का जलस्तर गिरता रहा तो देश के एकमात्र परमाणु ऊर्जा संयंत्र को पूरी तरह बंद करना पड़ सकता है।
पाक्स संयंत्र, जो अपने रिएक्टरों को ठंडा करने के लिए डेन्यूब नदी के पानी का उपयोग करता है, ने 3 अगस्त को अपनी सामान्य 2,000 मेगावाट बिजली के बजाय केवल 240 मेगावाट बिजली का उत्पादन किया। सोवियत संघ द्वारा निर्मित चार रिएक्टरों वाले इस संयंत्र का 44 वर्ष पहले परिचालन शुरू होने के बाद से पूर्णतः बंद होना अभूतपूर्व होगा। पाक्स संयंत्र हंगरी के लगभग आधे बिजली उत्पादन और लगभग एक तिहाई बिजली खपत के लिए जिम्मेदार है।
इसी बीच, पड़ोसी देश रोमानिया के बिजली संयंत्रों में भी बिजली उत्पादन में भारी गिरावट देखी गई, साथ ही साथ जहाजरानी और कृषि में भी व्यवधान उत्पन्न हुआ।
3 अगस्त को रोमानियाई सेना ने डेन्यूब नदी पर बाला नहर के पास चट्टानों को तोड़ने के लिए 180 किलोग्राम विस्फोटक का इस्तेमाल किया, ताकि नदी के मुख्य चैनल में पानी का रुख मोड़ा जा सके और उसे सरकारी स्वामित्व वाले चेर्नावोडा परमाणु ऊर्जा संयंत्र की ओर मोड़ा जा सके। रोमानिया ने पिछले सप्ताह एक रिएक्टर बंद कर दिया था और संभवतः दूसरा भी बंद कर देगा। यह पहली बार है जब रोमानिया को भीषण सूखे के कारण परमाणु रिएक्टर बंद करना पड़ा है। चेर्नावोडा परमाणु ऊर्जा संयंत्र में दो रिएक्टर हैं और यह रोमानिया की लगभग 20% बिजली की आपूर्ति करता है।
बिजली बचाना एक राष्ट्रीय नीति है।
पिछले सप्ताह, हंगरी सरकार ने एक आदेश जारी किया जिसमें बड़े औद्योगिक या वाणिज्यिक उपभोक्ताओं को बिजली बचाने के उपाय लागू करने का निर्देश दिया गया। 3 अगस्त से व्यस्त समय के दौरान इलेक्ट्रिक मालगाड़ियों के संचालन पर भी प्रतिबंध लगा दिया गया है। विशेष रूप से घरों से अनुरोध किया गया है कि वे स्वेच्छा से बिजली बचाएं, खासकर शाम 5 बजे से रात 10 बजे तक के व्यस्त समय के दौरान।
इस बीच, रोमानिया, जो कभी बिजली का एक प्रमुख निर्यातक था, आपूर्ति की कमी को पूरा करने के लिए यूक्रेन और पड़ोसी देशों से आपातकालीन बिजली आयात के लिए तत्काल बातचीत कर रहा है। 3 अगस्त को प्रमुख औद्योगिक ग्राहकों के साथ एक बैठक में, कार्यवाहक प्रधानमंत्री इली बोलोजान ने घोषणा की कि कार निर्माता कंपनियां डेसिया और फोर्ड रखरखाव मोड में चली गई हैं और 19 अगस्त तक कार उत्पादन निलंबित कर दिया है, जबकि अन्य कंपनियों ने व्यस्त समय के दौरान बिजली की खपत कम करने पर सहमति व्यक्त की है।

Temperatures are set to drop across the UK over the next few days, ending the latest heatwave that has affected some areas of southern and eastern England.
Humidity levels will fall too, which should cool down homes and make nights more comfortable for sleeping.
The change in conditions follows another historic day in a summer that has seen many long standing heat records toppled or tied. On Tuesday, the UK registered its 34th day of temperatures reaching 30C (86F) or higher in a calendar year, equalling the record set in 1995.
Forecasts suggest that this record is likely to be beaten as early as next week, with some showing the potential for a sixth heatwave to develop.
Thunderstorms and winds to blow away heat
A large area of low pressure crossing the UK has already brought areas of heavy and thundery rain to many northern and some western parts of the UK over the last few days.
More thunderstorms are expected in parts of north-east Scotland later on Wednesday.
The Met Office has issued a yellow warning, external between 13:00 and 21:00 BST. It warns of heavy, slow-moving showers and some thunderstorms breaking out from late morning.
Along with lightning, gusty winds and some hail, the storms will have the potential to produce up to 40mm of rain in a few places over three to six hours. This could lead to localised flash flooding and impact the transport network.
Later on in the day and into the night, unseasonably blustery winds will develop across parts of Scotland, Northern Ireland, the Isle of Man and northern England. Gales are possible on some hills and coasts.
Humidity levels to drop
Strengthening westerly winds will help to finally clear the higher humidity that has made recent days and nights uncomfortable at times.
Humidity is a measure of how much moisture is in the air.
During hot weather our body controls our internal temperature by sweating and as the sweat is evaporated from our skin, it cools the air directly next to us, making us feel cooler.
By Thursday, temperatures will sit between 15C and 24C across the UK. While this may feel distinctly cool for some after the recent hot weather, these temperatures are actually much closer to the August average.
For many in Scotland and Northern Ireland, it may actually feel like a more pleasant summer day, with few showers and more sunshine than in recent days.
Will there be another heatwave?
Some forecasts are already suggesting that temporary builds of high pressure and southerly winds across the parts of the country next week could lift some areas back above heatwave thresholds.
A few areas, especially in south-east England could again see temperatures above 30C.
The end of next week is still a long way off in forecasting terms, so it is not yet clear exactly how extensive any heat will be, how hot it will get and how long it will last.

A heat haze shimmers above a cement road in Yeongdeungpo District, western Seoul, on Aug. 4 as an extreme heat warning remains in effect across the capital.YONHAP
Seoul is bracing for a high of 39 degrees Celsius (102.2 degrees Fahrenheit) on Wednesday, as Tokyo — normally one of Asia’s hottest cities in the summer — stays under 30 degrees Celsius in a striking reversal of the two’s typical summer weather patterns.
Seoul reached 35.4 degrees Celsius as of noon on Wednesday, with the city’s daytime high expected to climb to 39 degrees Celsius, according to the Korea Meteorological Administration (KMA).
All of Seoul remains under a heat wave emergency warning, the highest level in Korea’s three-tier heat wave alert system.
The agency also issued heat wave emergency warnings on Wednesday for Gwangmyeong, Yeoncheon, Pocheon, Namyangju, Uiwang, and Hwaseong cities and Yangpyeong and Gapyeong counties in Gyeonggi; Cheongyang County in South Chungcheong; and southern Incheon. This marked the first time that a heat wave emergency warning had been issued anywhere in Chungcheong.
Including areas that had already had such measures in effect, 20 of the 46 land-based weather advisory zones across the greater Seoul area are now under a heat wave emergency warning. The remaining 26 zones issued a standard heat wave warning.
“Easterly winds will keep flowing into the greater Seoul area for the time being and push temperatures sharply higher,” a KMA official said. “Many areas will see highs of 39 degrees Celsius or above, bringing life-threatening levels of extreme heat.”
Tokyo, by contrast, is seeing weaker heat than usual for this time of year. According to the World Weather Information Service, the city is expected to stay cloudy on Wednesday, with a daytime high of just 28 degrees Celsius — more than 10 degrees cooler than Seoul.
Tokyo has traditionally been one of the region’s hottest cities, with an average August temperature of 31.3 degrees Celsius, higher than Seoul’s 30 degrees. But in recent years, Tokyo has seen a stretch of cool, autumn-like weather, with daytime highs staying below 30 degrees.
The sharp divergence between the two stems largely from surrounding pressure systems and wind patterns. In Seoul’s case, two high-pressure systems — the North Pacific High and the Tibetan High — have formed a heat dome over the region. Hot easterly winds, warmed as they cross the Taebaek Mountains, have only driven temperatures higher.
Tokyo, meanwhile, has been under the influence of the Okhotsk High, positioned northeast of Hokkaido, which has been pushing in a cold, damp northeasterly wind. This has caused Tokyo’s temperatures to drop sharply, as if the city skipped summer entirely and moved straight into early fall. Western Japan, including Kyushu, is seeing a very different picture, however, with extreme heat nearing 40 degrees Celsius, highlighting a stark east-west temperature divide within Japan.
Starting Thursday, Tokyo’s daytime temperatures are expected to climb back above 30 degrees Celsius. But Seoul is forecast to remain locked in extreme heat of up to 39 degrees Celsius through Thursday and Friday, so the heat gap between the two cities will likely persist for now.

Maxkamadda ayaa loo sheegay in Maxamed Maxamuud, oo 22 jir ah, uu u safray Soomaaliya isagoo isku dayaya inuu ku biiro 'koox argagixiso' ah mid ka mid ah goobaha ay ku xooggan yihiin, ka dib markii uu talo ka helay barnaamijkaas AI-ga ah.
Waxaa la sheegay inuu doonayay inuu noqdo qof u dhinta caqiidadiisa (shahiid), balse uu ku guuldareystay isku-daygii uu ugu biiri lahaa Islamic State, isla markaana la xiray markii uu dib ugu soo laabtay England.
Mr Maxamuud ayaa wajahaya dacwad ka socota Maxkamadda Winchester Crown Court ka dib markii uu beeniyay eedeymaha ku saabsan inuu diyaarinayay fal argagixiso ama falal argagixiso.
Maxkamadda ayaa maqashay in la-hadalka barnaamijyada AI-ga ay qayb ka ahaayeen habka lagu qiimeeyo dadka doonaya inay ku biiraan kooxda Daacish, oo sidoo kale loo yaqaan IS ama Isis.
'Wuxuu noqday qof xagjir ah oo aaminsan fikirka Islaamiga ah ee xad-dhaafka ah'.
Naomi Parsons oo ah qareenka dacwadda wada, ayaa ka hadashay Mr Maxamuud, kaas oo UK yimid sanadkii 2020 ama 2021 si uu ugu noolaado magaalada Bristol: "Waqti ka mid ah ayuu qaatay fikirka xagjirnimada. Dhinaca dacwadda ayaa sheegaya inuu noqday qof xagjir ah oo aaminsan fikirka Islaamiga ah ee xad-dhaafka ah, taasna ay keentay rabitaan ah inuu ku biiro Islamic State."
Waxay sheegtay in Mr Maxamuud uu "go'aansaday inuu ku biiro Islamic State oo ku sugan Soomaaliya" ka hor dhammaadka sanadka 2024, isla markaana, qayb ka mid ah habka uu ula xiriirayay kooxdaas uu "internet-ka u galay si uu ula hadlo barnaamijyada AI-ga", iyo sidoo kale dad dhab ah.
Ka dib markii uu internet-ka kula xiriiray qof, waxaa la sheegay inuu u sheegay: "Waxaan ahay wiil Soomaali ah oo ku nool England. Waxaan rabaa inaan u safro Boosaaso [magaalo ku taal waqooyi-bari Soomaaliya] si aan ugu biiro mujaahidiinta. Ma taqaan habka loo sameeyo socdaalka (hijrada)?"
Ereyga "Mujaahidiin" waxaa badanaa loo adeegsadaa dadka ka qaybqaata jihaadka.
Maxkamadda ayaa la horgeeyay xog sheegaysa in Mr Maxamuud uu goostay tigidh diyaaradeed oo dib ugu celinaya Soomaaliya, uuna halkaas u safray 30-kii Janaayo 2025-kii; wuxuuna la degay ayeeyadiis isagoo si joogto ah ula xiriirayay laba qof oo ka tirsan kooxda Daacish.
Ms Parsons ayaa sheegtay in markii uu Soomaaliya gaaray ka dib, uu Maxamuud la xiriirayay laba qof oo qaabilsan qorista xubnaha cusub, mid ka mid ah oo lagu magacaabo Abu Cali ayaa ku yiri: "Ma ogtahay inaan dhab ahaantii ku jirno xaalad dagaal?
"Ma ogtahay sida ay xaaladdu u cakiran tahay? Duqeymaha cirka ayaa sii socda, dagaal kululna wuu socdaa xilligan aan hadlayno. Ma la socotaa waxaas oo dhan?"
Mr Maxamuud ayaa la sheegay inuu ku jawaabay: "Haa walaal, si buuxda ayaan u ogahay. Runtii, waxaan aad u doonayaa inaan gaaro shahaado (dhimasho dagaal), mana jirto waqti ka wanaagsan kan hadda."
Si kastaba ha ahaatee, Ms Parsons ayaa sheegtay in loo sheegay in waddooyinka loogu biiro Daacish ay xiran yihiin dagaalka dartii, sidaas darteedna uu go'aansaday inuu dib ugu laabto UK 3-dii Maarso. Waxay sheegtay inuu sii waday xiriirkii uu la lahaa dadkaas qora xubnaha cusub, uuna ku yiri: "Wakhti kasta oo aad tiraahdaan, waan soo laabanayaa".
Maxkamadda ayaa la ogeysiiyay in isticmaalka joogtada ah ee uu eedaysanuhu u isticmaalayay taleefankiisa si uu u diro farriimo, u qaado sawirro, iyo inuu la hadlo barnaamijyada wada-hadalka ee AI (sirdoonka macmalka ah) ay bixisay xog badan oo ku saabsan dhaqdhaqaaqiisa.
Kooxda Daacish ee Soomaaliya, oo sidoo kale loo yaqaan IS-Somalia, waa koox dagaal-yahanno ah oo la aasaasay sanadkii 2015-kii, taas oo ka soo go'day koox kale oo argagixiso ah oo xiriir la lahayd Al-Qaacida.

Looking down on London's straw-coloured parks
July was officially the driest for England and Wales since records began 190 years ago.
With no recorded rainfall at the Kew Gardens weather station in July and the capital declared officially in drought amid a hosepipe ban, the impact on London's formerly green spaces is clear for all to see: a slew of straw-coloured expanses across the city.
Who better to capture this phenomenon than photographer Jason Hawkes, who has been flying in the skies above London capturing snapshots for more than 35 years?
"It's quite interesting to see how different it does look, compared to one month ago," he says.
"I don't think I've ever seen Hyde Park look so barren – it looks mental from the air," the 58-year-old says.
"The rooftop terraces are still really green so are an interesting juxtaposition."
Which is his favourite shot of summer in the city?
"I like the viewing point at Primrose Hill," he says. "Normally that's incredibly green there – it's mad. It's incredible."
Hawkes adds: "It was quite similar four years ago but everywhere is like it now in the South East.
"The rooftop terraces are the only things that stay green – they hardly ever seem to get used."
The heatwaves have provided one benefit for the photographer while he carries out his work.
"It's quite nice because normally it's freezing – I can wear shorts," he says.
"The helicopters haven't changed much but everything else has, including the kit," the photographer says about his time doing the job.

Dakota Gardener: Helping gardens survive extreme heat
There are a few irrigation tips to relieve stress
Trending
Yikes! It is hot - dangerously hot. Our plants in the garden are wilting, and we are soaked in sweat trying to care for them.
My cucumber and zucchini vines droop every afternoon. The initial harvest was great, but production is slowing down due to the extreme heat. The vines are producing fewer female (fruit-bearing) flowers. The pollen from the male flowers is less effective in this heat, too.
Bees don't like this scorching heat. They are seeking shade and becoming less active pollinating our crops.
The combination of fewer female flowers, poor pollen and reduced bee activity will lead to a short-term reduction in production. I expect some of my next flush of cucumbers will be curled and misshapen because of insufficient pollination.
Our tomatoes are suffering. When temperatures exceed 85 degrees Fahrenheit daily, tomato flowers may wither before setting fruits. Tomato fruits on the vine will be slower to redden and ripen.
We expect an uptick in more tomato fruits suffering from blossom end rot. This rot at the bottom of fruits is caused by a lack of calcium. Hot, dry conditions reduce soil moisture. When soil moisture is low, less calcium flows from the soil into the fruits, causing more blossom end rot.
Many peppers are getting sunburned. These scalded fruits are found on smaller plants that lack the foliage to shade the fruits.
One way to combat excessive heat is to shade our plants. Shade cloth can be hung over them. Container plants can be moved to shady areas.
Adding mulch will conserve soil moisture. Be sure the mulch, whether it be straw or grass clippings, was not treated with herbicide.
Most of us respond to our wilting plants by irrigating them. Let's discuss the proper way to irrigate your plants.
First, it is better to irrigate deeply and infrequently rather than giving your plants a sip of water every day. Roots grow where the water is. If you irrigate deeply, the roots of the plants will grow deeply. That's what we want.
Next, irrigate in the morning after sunrise. Plants in the morning absorb the water they need, and their leaves will dry quickly. Avoid mid-day irrigation because you will lose much of the water from evaporation. Avoid watering at night because prolonged periods of wet leaves will lead to disease.
Do not use overhead irrigation. Why do we irrigate the leaves of a plant? A plant drinks primarily through its roots, not leaves. We should irrigate the roots. Wet leaves lead to disease.
This reminds me of my first job: a sunflower killer at Northrup King Seed Company. The scientists at the company trained me to kill as many sunflower plants as possible with diseases. The goal was to discover a disease-resistant variety that I could not kill.
I grew diseases in the laboratory during the day and then sprinkled the disease spores on the plants at night. Then I turned on the overhead sprinklers. The presence of diseases along with wet leaves at night was a deadly combination.
This deadly combination continues to work today. There is a huge outbreak of blight now on tomato and potato vines in my community garden. My fellow gardeners tell me this happens every year.
That's because most of them wet the leaves of their plants when watering. Don't do that! Instead, use a watering wand or soaker hose. Direct the water at the roots of the plants and keep the leaves dry.
Plants in our gardens are wilting today, but they can recover with your help. Irrigate early in the day, irrigate deeply and keep the leaves dry. Once this heat wave cools off, you may be rewarded with a bountiful harvest.
(Tom Kalb is a horticulturist with North Dakota State Univeristy Extension.)

The Dehradun district administration has declared a one-day holiday for all government and private schools, as well as Anganwadi centres, on Wednesday following the India Meteorological Department’s forecast of heavy rainfall.
The closure applies to all schools from Classes 1 to 12 and all Anganwadi centres across the district.
Amid the prevailing weather conditions, Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami directed the Secretary of Disaster Management, the State Disaster Response Force (SDRF), the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), and district administrations to remain on high alert and ensure prompt relief and rescue operations in case of any emergency.
The Chief Minister also appealed to residents and tourists to avoid unnecessary travel and undertake journeys only if essential. He urged people to stay away from rivers, streams and other vulnerable areas and to strictly follow advisories issued by local authorities.
Heavy rainfall since late Tuesday night has led to a sharp rise in the water level of the Tamsa River flowing through the Tapkeshwar Mahadev Temple in Dehradun.
The India Meteorological Department has issued an Orange Alert for several districts, including Dehradun, Bageshwar, Tehri Garhwal and Uttarkashi, forecasting thunderstorms accompanied by lightning, heavy rainfall and gusty winds.
Earlier this week, Chief Minister Dhami directed officials to restore the road connecting Khainuri village in Chamoli district after it was damaged in a landslide, disrupting connectivity for around 120 families. He instructed the district administration to carry out restoration work on priority and ensure the early resumption of traffic.
-ANI
